renders._yaml:
- component: advanced_viz
  id: duplication_vs_depth
  title: Duplication rate against depth
  description: |-
    Each point is a library: the reads left after duplicate removal (horizontal) against its duplication rate (vertical), sized by the number of duplicates. It answers whether a library is deep because it is rich or only because it is duplicated.
    How to read: a point high and to the left is a library that is mostly duplicates with little unique data left, so more sequencing buys little. A point low and to the right is a complex library. The cited Picard metric definitions state no cut-off for an acceptable duplication rate.
    Lines and annotations: The dashed line is the median duplication rate of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of Picard.
    Source: https://broadinstitute.github.io/picard/picard-metric-definitions.html
  kind: scatter_xy
  config:
    x_title: Reads left after duplicate removal
    y_title: Duplication rate (fraction of mapped reads)
    legend_pos: bottom
    reference_line: horizontal
    reference_stat: median
  roles:
    x: reads_after_dedup
    y: percent_duplication
    label: sample
    color: sample
    size: duplicate_reads

- component: figure
  title: Duplication rate per library
  description: |-
    Each bar is a library: the fraction of its mapped sequence that MarkDuplicates flagged as duplicate. It answers which libraries are the most duplicated.
    How to read: a tall bar is a library with low molecular complexity, common with low-input or ancient DNA. Compare it with the complexity curve to see whether deeper sequencing would add new molecules.
    Lines and annotations: The dashed line is the median duplication rate of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of Picard.
    Source: https://broadinstitute.github.io/picard/picard-metric-definitions.html
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: sample
    y: percent_duplication
    color: sample
    title: Duplication rate per library
    labels:
      sample: Library
      percent_duplication: Duplication rate (fraction of mapped reads)
  reference_lines:
  - axis: y
    stat: median
    column: percent_duplication

- component: card
  title: Duplication rate
  description: |-
    The hero number is the mean duplication rate, a fraction between 0 and 1, with the spread across libraries in the box. It answers how much of the data is redundant.
    How to read: a wide box means libraries of very different complexity. A high mean means resequencing will mostly return duplicates. The cited Picard metric definitions state no cut-off for this rate.
    Source: https://broadinstitute.github.io/picard/picard-metric-definitions.html
  column: percent_duplication
  aggregation: average
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: mean, with the spread

- component: card
  title: Duplicate reads
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total of reads flagged as duplicates (unpaired plus both reads of each duplicate pair), with the median and the largest library next to it. It answers how much sequencing was spent on duplicates.
    How to read: a maximum far above the median is a library that wasted most of its reads. Compare it with the duplication rate to separate a deep library from a duplicated one.
  column: duplicate_reads
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: compact
  caption: per library, the median and the largest

- component: card
  title: Reads after duplicate removal
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total of examined reads left once duplicates are removed, with the median and the smallest library next to it. It answers how much unique data the downstream analysis has.
    How to read: the smallest library is the one that limits a joint analysis. Coverage downstream rests on this number rather than the raw depth.
  column: reads_after_dedup
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - median
  - min
  secondary_layout: compact
  caption: per library, the median and the smallest

- component: card
  title: Single-end reads examined
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total of single-end reads MarkDuplicates examined, with the median and the largest library next to it. It answers how much input the duplication rate rests on.
    How to read: collapsed or single-end libraries report their reads here, while paired libraries report read pairs in the table.
    Source: https://broadinstitute.github.io/picard/picard-metric-definitions.html
  column: unpaired_reads_examined
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: compact
  caption: per library, the median and the largest

- component: table
  title: Duplication metrics per library
  description: |-
    Each row is a library: the reads examined, the duplicates flagged, the reads left after removal, the duplication rate and Picard's library size estimate. It answers how redundant each library is.
    How to read: the estimated library size is the number of unique molecules Picard infers from the paired duplicates, and is empty when it cannot be estimated.
    Source: https://broadinstitute.github.io/picard/picard-metric-definitions.html
